The definition has the stated Fighter_GObj pointer signature and accesses the specified input, frame, persistent charge and move-local fields.

The aerial B, L/R and frame-zero conditions are sequential independent checks without an early return or grounded common-action guard. The proposal correctly describes possibility rather than guaranteeing both transitions.
Grounded IASA contains the negated ftCo_8009917C guard, pressed-button tests, charge transfer and independent cancellation processing exactly as described.
The grounded definition confirms the signature and pressed-button category; no held-input interpretation is needed.
A true common-action result skips the move-local body. Within that body release has no early return, preserving subsequent latch and cancellation checks.
Aerial startup completion selects the aerial loop at frame zero and rate one. Independently inspected inline code only installs death, damage and effect-hitlag callbacks.
The startup caller and inline definition support transition plus callback restoration, not collision reconciliation.

Aerial release confirms the effect latch, air-dependent effect selection, shared hitbox-0 guard, two damage caches, charge clearing and zero/nonzero recovery branches. Charge accumulation and separate hat.kind dispatch establish that xBC is not the copied-ability flag.

Grounded release confirms separate effect and movement latches, hitbox-0 gating of both damage updates, facing-relative charge-scaled ground velocity and completion cleanup. The proposal preserves delegation to ft_8008A2BC instead of claiming unconditional Wait.
